discover:people.current_state:
The Members tab on all three apps is a dashboard of one member's stats. It is not a list of people. Web `apps/web/src/app/members/page.tsx:44-49` works out the role. Admins get a metrics preview and a "View as" picker for any member (:281). Loggers can view-as only other members' Recent and Health cards (:363). Plain members see only their own cards (:411) plus a "View Members" pill (:262). iOS does the same (`Features/Home/AdminHomeView.swift:73-75`; `Tabs/StandardMembersTab.swift:70-79`), and so does Android (`ui/members/MembersScreen.kt:79-83,147-182`).

The roster screens are web `members/list/page.tsx`, iOS `ProgramManagement/MemberManagementSection.swift:65-96` and Android `ui/members/MemberManagementScreens.kt:153-188`. Each row shows initials, name, @username and an admin star. Only a global admin can tap a row (web :64, iOS :70-72, Android :155,188), and the tap opens the membership editor. There are no photos (initials only, `MemberCards.kt:122`) and no storage bucket.

**Profile:** the `members` table holds username, first and last name, gender, global_role, status and created_at (`sql/001_schema.sql:24-34`). There is no bio, photo or settings column.

**Activity:** `workout_logs` has a composite key (program, member, workout type, date) plus duration and created_at (`001_schema.sql:110-119`). `daily_health_logs` holds sleep, diet and steps, with a source per field (migrations 006 and 009:88-91). Streaks are computed on the fly (`memberAnalyticsService.js:28-48`), and "current streak" does not reset when today has no log.

**Who can read what today:**
- Any active member can read any co-member's metrics, history, streaks and recent workouts. `ensureProgramAccess` only checks the person asking (`memberAnalyticsService.js:6-26`).
- The metrics response includes every member's average sleep, diet and steps (:115-124,215-220).
- Raw health rows are limited to yourself, admins and loggers (`logService.js:735-738`). But `/analytics/health/timeline` and `/health/steps` accept any memberId (`routes/analytics.js:102-121`).
- The roster endpoints never check that the caller is in the program (`membershipService.js:122-172`).
- `GET /members/:id` returns any member's email (`memberService.js:25-45`), and `GET /members` lists every standard member in the app (:16-23).
- Plain members' apps already download the full leaderboard and keep only their own row (`StandardMembersTab.swift:175-184`; `MembersScreen.kt:164-165`).

**Blocking:** exists only per program. "Block future invites" on decline writes `program_invite_blocks(program_id, member_id)` (`inviteService.js:234-235`, checked at `inviteSendService.js:50-53`). There is no unblock screen, prod has 2 rows, and you cannot block a person.

**Other:** notifications only cover `program.*` events (`specs/features/notifications/SPEC.md:214-215`). There are no kudos and no preferences table. The Members screens don't use the frontend kit yet, so load errors are silently dropped.

**Prod (read-only, 2026-10-13):** 23 programs, 60 members, 166 active memberships, largest program 30 people. Roles: 47 admin, 7 logger, 112 member. 35 members are in 2+ programs, and 14 logged a workout in the last 7 days.
gaps_vs_concept: No People list a plain member can use: the roster exists on all 3 surfaces, but rows only open for a global admin, and a program admin's Members tab has no roster button (web members/page.tsx:262 shows 'View Members' only when !canViewAs).
No profile screen for another member. The data already exists and the backend already serves it to any co-member (memberAnalyticsService.js:18-26), so most of the work is on the clients.
No program activity feed. Recent workouts are only fetched one member at a time (member-recent). workout_logs.created_at exists, but no endpoint lists a program's recent activity.

No kudos: no table, no endpoint, no notification type (only program.* types exist, notifications SPEC:214-215). The notification redesign's categories and preferences (DESIGN_BOARD §9) aren't built yet.
No 'hide my activity' switch: no column or preferences table (001_schema.sql:24-34). It has to be enforced on the server, because plain-member apps already download every member's metrics.

'Visible only to people in your programs' is not true today. GET /members/:id leaks any member's email (memberService.js:25-45). GET /members lists every standard member in the app (memberService.js:16-23). The roster endpoints don't check the caller is in the program (membershipService.js:122-172).

Health data is gated inconsistently: raw daily-health-logs are self or staff only (logService.js:735-738), but any co-member can get averages through member-metrics (avg_sleep_hours/avg_food_quality/avg_steps) and /analytics/health/timeline|steps with any memberId (routes/analytics.js:102-121).

Blocking exists only per program (program_invite_blocks) and only when declining an invite. There is no person-to-person block and no unblock screen. Because People only shows people in programs you're in, today's block never overlaps with People, so 'extend blocking to People' has no meaning until a person-level block exists.
No photos (initials only on all 3) and no storage bucket. Profile fields are limited to name, @username, gender and created_at.
The Members screens haven't adopted the frontend kit (errors dropped, no Retry, no offline view), unlike Summary and Programs. People would be built on the kit.

decisions.question: D-P1 How big is People in v1: one program or across programs?
decisions.options: (a) Per program: the active program's members, inside the Members tab. (b) Everyone you share any program with (35 of 60 members are in 2+ programs).
decisions.recommendation: (a). It matches today's program-scoped tabs and the concept ('everyone in a program you share'). Cross-program can come later.

decisions.question: D-P2 Where People lives and how much of the Members tab changes
decisions.options: (a) Additive: the existing roster becomes the People list, reachable from a header button for every role (admins too), and every row opens a profile. The dashboard and view-as stay as they are. (b) Rebuild the tab: your own summary on top, the People list below, and tapping a person replaces the view-as picker (staff see the full stat cards on that person's profile). (c) A new 5th tab.
decisions.recommendation: (a) for v1. It is the least work, doesn't restyle the page (new-UI rule) and still makes Members grow into People. Keep (b) as a later polish candidate if (a) gets used: it removes three role branches and the view-as storage code on each app, but it is a page rebuild on all three. Not (c). Keep the tab name 'Members'.

decisions.question: D-P3 What 'recent activity' shows on a profile
decisions.options: (a) Workouts only: current and longest streak, active days this month, the last ~10 workouts (type, duration, date), last active date. All from existing member-analytics data. (b) (a) plus steps. (c) (a) plus sleep, diet and steps. (d) Also a program-wide feed of recent activity (new endpoint over workout_logs.created_at).
decisions.recommendation: (a). Workouts are already visible to co-members on the backend. Sleep and diet are deliberately staff-only today. Leave the feed (d) for later; it fits the notification redesign's Activity category.

decisions.question: D-P4 Kudos in v1?
decisions.options: (a) No kudos: People is a list plus profiles. (b) Minimal kudos: one tap per giver per member-day, can be undone, a count on the profile, no text. The receiver gets an in-app notification, and a push only if their Activity notifications are on. (c) Kudos plus comments or reactions.
decisions.recommendation: (b). Without kudos, People is just a roster with stats, and kudos is the one social piece. Keeping it text-free avoids App Store user-generated-content rules (filtering, reporting). Ship it after the notification redesign so it can use that category switch; until then it's in-app only.

decisions.question: D-P5 What a kudos is attached to
decisions.options: (a) A member-day: (program, receiver, date), unique per giver. (b) A single workout row. workout_logs has no id of its own (composite key incl. type and date), so editing the type or date breaks the link, and health sync sums several workouts into one row. (c) Add an id column to workout_logs first.
decisions.recommendation: (a). It survives edits and health sync, needs one small table, and reads naturally ('kudos for Tuesday').

decisions.question: D-P6 Who can see your activity by default
decisions.options: (a) Visible to co-members by default, with a per-member 'Hide my activity' switch (the concept). (b) Hidden by default; members opt in.
decisions.recommendation: (a). It matches what the backend already allows and the approved concept. (b) would leave People mostly empty.

decisions.question: D-P7 What 'Hide my activity' hides, and from whom
decisions.options: (a) One switch per member (all programs). It hides your stats, workouts and kudos button on People and member-analytics reads from plain co-members. You stay on the list by name. Staff (program admin, logger, global admin) still see everything, because they run the program and log for others. Program-wide totals still count you. (b) Same, but also hidden from staff. (c) One switch per program.
decisions.recommendation: (a). (b) breaks admin dashboards and logging for others, and (c) adds settings screens for no real gain. Store it as a boolean column on `members` (migration 011, idempotent), or in the notification preferences table if that lands first. Enforce it with one shared server check used by every per-member read.

decisions.question: D-P8 Close today's privacy leaks before People ships?
decisions.options: (a) Yes, backend-only, before People: GET /members/:id returns email only to yourself or a global admin; GET /members (all members) is global-admin only; roster endpoints require the caller to be in the program; other people's health averages are nulled for plain members and health timeline/steps memberId is limited to yourself or staff (matching daily-health-logs). (b) Fix only the email leak. (c) Leave as is.
decisions.recommendation: (a). People advertises 'visible only to people in your programs', and today that isn't true. Every change keeps the response shapes. Plain-member apps only display their own row, so live binaries are unaffected (a plan must re-check each caller). This also fits the polish round.

decisions.question: D-P9 Person-to-person blocking in v1?
decisions.options: (a) No new blocking. People only shows co-members. The privacy tools are 'Hide my activity' and leaving the program. Today's per-program invite block stays, plus optionally an 'Unblocked programs' list in account settings. (b) A person-level block table: the blocked person can't see your activity, give you kudos or invite you. You both still share the roster and logging pickers. (c) Mute kudos from someone.
decisions.recommendation: (a). Programs average about 4 people and are formed by invitation, so a person-level block is over-engineering now. If kudos ever gets text or photos, App Store guideline 1.2 makes (b) mandatory; revisit then.

decisions.question: D-P10 Profile photos
decisions.options: (a) Initials only (today). (b) Photo upload to Supabase Storage (new bucket, size limits, moderation and reporting duties).
decisions.recommendation: (a). Photos bring user-generated-content and moderation obligations, and a new bucket, for little benefit in programs of people who already know each other.

decisions.question: D-P11 What each role sees on a profile
decisions.options: (a) Everyone can open any co-member's profile. Plain members see the D-P3 summary (or 'activity hidden'). Staff also get an 'Open full stats' link into the existing member detail screens. Membership editing stays global-admin only (faithful). (b) Also let program admins edit memberships from the profile (the backend already allows it).
decisions.recommendation: (a) for v1, since it changes no admin flows. (b) is a cheap polish item if admins ask for it.

build_slices: S0 (backend only, S): privacy hardening per D-P8. Email only for yourself or a global admin; GET /members global-admin only; roster endpoints check the caller's membership; others' health averages nulled for plain members; health timeline/steps memberId limited to yourself or staff. Shapes unchanged; staging smoke plus a check of each live-binary caller. Independent of People; can ride the polish round.

S1 (backend, M): migration 011 (members.hide_activity boolean default false; kudos table (program_id, giver_id, receiver_id, log_date, created_at) with a unique key on all four ids/date and FKs to program_memberships). GET /api/people?programId returns the roster plus last active date, current streak and active days this month, with hidden members' stats null for non-staff (one call). GET /api/people/:memberId?programId returns the profile (role, joined, streak, active days, last 10 workouts, kudos per day, whether I gave). PUT/DELETE /api/people/kudos, rate-limited per giver. PUT /members/:id whitelist gains hide_activity. One canSeeActivity(requester, target, program) check applied to member-metrics, history, streaks, recent and the analytics memberId reads. A kudos sends notification type activity.kudos through createNotification.

S2 (web, M): /members/list becomes the People list (every row opens a profile; built on the kit; 'You' pinned at the top). New /members/person profile page with a kudos button. 'Hide my activity' toggle on /program/profile. Members tab header gets a People button for every role. Must fit mobile and desktop.

S3 (iOS, M, parallel with S4): ProgramMembersListView becomes the People list with a NavigationLink for every role. New PersonProfileView with kudos. Toggle in MyProfileView. People button on both Members tab variants. Uses the kit (LoadState / ErrorStateView / FloatingBanner). Compile check is the user's ⌘B (tools/ios-typecheck.sh first).

S4 (Android, M, parallel with S3): ProgramMembersListScreen becomes the People list. New PERSON route using the focusMember idiom, plus a PersonProfileScreen with kudos. Toggle in ProfileScreen. Neutral M3 surfaces, kit ErrorView/FloatingBanner. assembleDebug clean.
S5 (all 3, S, can fold into S2-S4): move the Members tab dashboard onto the kit (stop dropping errors; stale banner and Retry; pull-to-refresh on mobile).

S6 (docs, S, with S1): new `people` feature SPEC (D-P1..D-P11 as §9 D-rules), plus updates to the members, member-analytics, program-memberships and analytics SPECs (privacy changes), the page SPECs, registry.json and REGISTRY.md. Then git-version.
S7 (later, optional, L): Members tab rebuild per D-P2(b), where tapping a person replaces the view-as picker. Only if v1 People gets used.
risks: Scope relative to what the user asked for right now: the user's message is about the iPhone offline indicator and holding store submission until the polish round, and that is already planned in specs/initiatives/reliability-overhaul/plans/polish-1-offline-detection.md. People is a Phase 4 feature after the notification redesign. It shouldn't delay or join the pre-submission polish build; only S0 (backend-only privacy fixes) fits that window.

Hide-activity leak risk: per-member data comes from many endpoints (member-metrics/history/streaks/recent, analytics health timeline/steps and workout types with memberId, summary top_performers at analyticsService.js:198-205,253). Missing one makes the switch a lie, so it needs one shared server check and a test listing every route.

Store and health-data policy: People shows workouts synced from HealthKit and Health Connect to other members. Apple 5.1.3 and Google's Health Connect policy need clear consent and disclosure, so update the in-app consent copy, the privacy policy page (specs/pages/web/privacy-policy) and the App Store and Play data-safety answers ('visible to members of your programs'). Text kudos, comments or photos would trigger App Store guideline 1.2 (filter, report, block).

Live-binary compatibility for S0: must keep response shapes and must not 403 any flow old iOS 1.4.x / 1.5.0 or Android 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 needs (e.g. iOS loadLookupData calls GET /members when no program is selected, ProgramContext+Members.swift:20-24). The plan must list every caller per binary in RELEASES.md.

Kudos depends on the notification redesign (categories, preferences, member time zones for what 'today' means). Shipping kudos first means either no notification or a quick emit that gets redone. Keep the BRIEF §7 order (notifications, then People).

Kudos keyed to a member-day can go stale: if every workout that day is deleted or moved to another date, the kudos points at an empty day. Hide kudos on days with no workouts instead of cascading deletes.

'Current streak' doesn't reset when today has no log (member-analytics F2). A People profile will show stale streaks to co-members, which looks wrong socially. Fixing it changes every streak number (a deliberate change that needs its own decision).

Effort: three client implementations plus the iOS ⌘B loop. The new profile screen must meet the standing UI rules (fits and responsive on web mobile and desktop, iOS centered column on iPad, Android neutral M3, any chart needs a tooltip). Keep v1 chart-free to avoid that.
Low scale (max roster 30, 60 members) means pagination and caching aren't needed. Don't build them.

discover:notifications.current_state:
BACKEND. One emit engine: createNotification (apps/backend/utils/notifications.js:43-96) writes notifications + notification_recipients. After commit it sends over SSE and calls sendPushToMembers (utils/pushNotifications.js:58-90): one token query, APNs + FCM in parallel, prune, then one push_deliveries row per attempt plus no_device (:86). APNs note = alert + sound + custom keys with 7-day expiry, but no badge and no thread-id (utils/push/apns.js:58-66). FCM picks rasi_invites or rasi_default by type (utils/push/fcm.js:10-17,54). Routes (routes/notifications.js): GET /unacknowledged (:24-53, unread only, no paging), POST /:id/acknowledge (:140-160), the device routes, the vestigial /broadcast (:104-138) and SSE /stream (:162-188).

Emitting types, all about programs: invite_received (services/inviteSendService.js:74), member_joined (inviteService.js:171,212), role_changed (membershipService.js:266; utils/programMemberships.js:116), member_removed (membershipService.js:331), member_left (membershipService.js:414; programMemberships.js:215), admin_transferred (programMemberships.js:131), program.deleted when the last member leaves (programMemberships.js:79). program.updated/deleted from programService still go to a no-op stub (services/programService.js:20-23,176,210).

Schema: notifications/recipients have no category, no read_at (acknowledged_at doubles as read), no dedupe key and no retention (sql/001_schema.sql:214-236; the sql/010 crons only prune push_deliveries and tokens). members has no time zone (001:24-39), and no client sends one (utils/clientInfo.js:4-10; middleware/requestLog.js:41 logs only cf-ipcountry). There is no scheduler (package.json; one Render starter instance).

CLIENTS. All three show a blocking modal queue, one notification at a time: web NotificationsGate.tsx:51-307 (mounted at shell.tsx:60), iOS AppRootView.swift:32-41 + ProgramContext+Notifications.swift, Android RootScreen.kt:129-136 + ProgramContext.kt:560-664. No surface has an inbox or history. Web has no notifications page (programs/page.tsx:474-521). The settings screens show OS permission only: iOS NotificationsSettingsView.swift asks only from its button (:159-170) or when Apple Health is connected (HealthKitSyncNotifier.swift:16-21); Android asks once after the first sign-in (RootScreen.kt:79-90). The only badge is the invite count on the picker '+' button (web programs/page.tsx:254-257; iOS ProgramPickerView.swift:531). iOS willPresent passes .badge (AppDelegate.swift:61-65), but no payload sets one. Android uses the launcher mipmap as the small icon (RaSiFirebaseMessagingService.kt:51), and the manifest has no default_notification_icon (AndroidManifest.xml:85-88).

PROD (read-only, today): 512 notifications since 2026-02-09, 105 in the last 90 days (invite_received 46, member_joined 38 reaching 245 recipients, member_left 10, role_changed 9, admin_transferred 2, program.updated 0). 333 unread rows across 30 members, up to 51 for one member. 22 of 60 members have a device (10 iOS, 19 Android tokens). 7 push_deliveries rows so far.
gaps_vs_concept: CATEGORIES: there are none. Only `type` strings exist. The only grouping is FCM's two-channel split (apps/backend/utils/push/fcm.js:12-17). Notifications and push payloads carry no `category`, and APNs has no `thread-id` (utils/push/apns.js:58-66).

PREFERENCES: there is no per-member preference table or route. iOS pages SPEC F2 says so (specs/pages/ios/notifications/SPEC.md:94). The settings screens only show OS permission (NotificationsSettingsView.swift; Android NotificationsScreen.kt). Web has no notifications settings page at all.

INBOX: none. Only GET /unacknowledged exists (routes/notifications.js:24-53: unread only, oldest first, no paging) plus a blocking modal queue on every surface. Once you dismiss a notification you can never see it again. There is no unread count, no mark-all-read and no history on web, iOS or Android.

READ/UNREAD: `acknowledged_at` is the only state, so 'dismissed the modal' and 'read' are the same thing. The backlog is 333 unread rows across 30 members, up to 51 for one member, so that member would see 51 modals in a row.
90-DAY HISTORY: the notifications table has no retention job (sql/010 prunes only push_deliveries and tokens). Rows go back to 2026-02-09, and 407 of the 512 are older than 90 days.

TIME ZONE: missing. members has no column (sql/001_schema.sql:24-39). The client headers carry platform/version/build only (utils/clientInfo.js:4-10), and the request log has only the country (requestLog.js:41), which is not enough for the US or Canada.

SCHEDULER: none (no cron dependency in package.json, no Render cron, no pg_cron job that sends anything). There is also no dedupe key, which an idempotent 'one reminder per member per local day' needs.
ENGAGEMENT TYPES: reminders, streak-at-risk and digest don't exist. Streaks are computed only for analytics (services/memberAnalyticsService.js:28-48, and not relative to 'today').

PROGRAM UPDATES: program.updated and program.deleted from the edit/delete routes still go to a no-op stub (services/programService.js:20-23). The concept's 'program updated/deleted' is not live: 0 sent in 90 days.

BADGES: there is no app-icon badge. APNs sends no `badge` and the iOS app never calls setBadgeCount. The only in-app badge is the pending-invite count on the picker '+' button (web programs/page.tsx:254-257).

PERMISSION COVERAGE: iOS never asks at sign-in. It asks only from the settings button or when Apple Health is connected, while Android asks once after the first sign-in (RootScreen.kt:79-90). Only 22 of 60 members have a device (10 iOS tokens vs 19 Android).

ANDROID CHANNELS AND ICON: only rasi_default and rasi_invites exist (App.kt:21-37), so a member can't mute reminders separately in system settings. The small icon is the launcher mipmap (RaSiFirebaseMessagingService.kt:51, HealthSyncNotifier.kt:49), and there is no default_notification_icon meta-data, so background pushes show a blob in the status bar.

DELIVERY RECORDS: every server push is already recorded in push_deliveries (pushNotifications.js:86). The local Apple Health / Health Connect sync notifications (HealthKitSyncNotifier.swift, HealthSyncNotifier.kt) are device-only: they skip both preferences and push_deliveries.
WEB CHANNEL: there is no web push (D-11), so on web a reminder or digest can only appear in the inbox.
BROADCAST: POST /broadcast is vestigial and global-admin only (F1). There is no announcements category, and any future announcement would count as promotional (opt-in).

decisions.question: D-N1 Which categories ship in v1?
decisions.options: (a) All 4 from the concept now: Program & invites, Activity, Reminders, Digest. (b) 3 now (Program & invites, Reminders, Digest); Activity arrives with the People layer, since nothing produces activity events today. (c) 2 now (Program & invites, Reminders); Digest is the next slice once the scheduler is proven, Activity comes with People.
decisions.recommendation: (c). Shipping a switch that controls nothing is effort for no benefit. Reminders are a cheap daily rule; Digest needs a content job and reuses the same scheduler later. member_joined/member_left stay in Program & invites, which is how they behave today.

decisions.question: D-N2 What does turning a category off actually stop?
decisions.options: (a) Every channel: the notification is never created. (b) Push and the live pop-up only; the inbox always records it. (c) Mixed: Program & invites off = push off but still in the inbox (it's transactional, and invites must stay reachable); Reminders/Digest off = never generated.
decisions.recommendation: (c). It keeps 'honoured by every channel' for the engagement categories while never hiding membership facts or invites. Filter once, centrally, in createNotification and the scheduler, so no call site changes.

decisions.question: D-N3 How should new notifications appear in the app?
decisions.options: (a) Keep the blocking modal queue and add an inbox. (b) Replace the modal with a floating toast ('Role updated - View') plus the inbox and an unread badge. (c) Modal only for invites, toast for everything else.
decisions.recommendation: (b). One member has 51 unread notifications, which means 51 modals in a row. A toast floats and doesn't restyle any page (standing rule). Invites are still one tap away in the inbox.

decisions.question: D-N4 Where does the inbox live?
decisions.options: (a) A bell icon in screen headers (breaks 'never add buttons to iOS custom headers'). (b) Grow the program picker's existing actions sheet 'My Invites' tab into 'Inbox' (pending invites on top, 90-day history below). The existing '+' button badge becomes unread + invites, and an 'Inbox' row goes in the in-program account section. (c) A new bottom tab.
decisions.recommendation: (b). It reuses the sheet, tab and badge that already exist on all three surfaces (web programs/page.tsx:254-257,408-421; iOS ProgramPickerView; Android picker actions sheet), so it adds no new chrome and converges rather than inventing.

decisions.question: D-N5 What does 'read' mean?
decisions.options: (a) Reuse acknowledged_at as read, so dismissing a modal on an old app = read and nothing changes for live binaries. (b) Add a separate read_at column.
decisions.recommendation: (a). No migration of semantics, and old iOS 1.4.2 / Android 1.0.0 stay correct. Add GET /notifications (paged, 90 days, read flag, unread_count) and POST /notifications/read-all next to the existing /:id/acknowledge.

decisions.question: D-N6 How do we get each member's time zone?
decisions.options: (a) Automatically: every new client sends its IANA zone in an X-Time-Zone header, and the server stores it on members only when it changes (validated against the IANA list). (b) An explicit time-zone picker in My Profile. (c) Infer it from the request country.
decisions.recommendation: (a). No UI, it follows people who travel, and it covers web too. (c) is wrong for the US and Canada. Members on old binaries simply get no reminders until they update, which is fine because only new builds can opt in.

decisions.question: D-N7 When is the daily reminder sent?
decisions.options: (a) A fixed 19:00 local time. (b) The member picks a time (default 19:00) using the native picker. (c) A smart time learned from when they usually log.
decisions.recommendation: (b). This is what fitness apps normally do, and it's small: one column plus a native time picker on each surface. (c) is over-engineering.

decisions.question: D-N8 What is the reminder rule?
decisions.options: (a) One daily reminder, sent only if nothing was logged today (local date, any active program, synced workouts included). When the current streak is 2 or more, the copy changes to 'Keep your N-day streak'. (b) Separate 'log' and 'streak' reminders with separate switches.
decisions.recommendation: (a). One switch and at most one push per day. Streak-at-risk is just different copy, not a second notification.

decisions.question: D-N9 What runs the scheduler?
decisions.options: (a) A ticker inside the API (every 15 min) that picks members whose local reminder time falls in the window and haven't been sent today, made idempotent by a unique notifications.dedupe_key (e.g. reminder:<member>:<local date>). (b) Supabase pg_cron + pg_net calling a secret-protected endpoint. (c) A separate Render Cron Job service.
decisions.recommendation: (a). No new infrastructure, secret or bill. The dedupe key prevents a double send even after a deploy restart or with a second instance. A missed tick catches up inside the window.

decisions.question: D-N10 How are preferences stored?
decisions.options: (a) A new notification_preferences table with one row per member: program bool (default true), reminders bool (default false), digest bool (default false), reminder_time, updated_at. (b) A JSONB column on members. (c) One row per (member, category).
decisions.recommendation: (a). Typed defaults, one-join queries for the scheduler, and adding a category is a one-line migration. Missing row = defaults. GET/PUT /notifications/preferences.

decisions.question: D-N11 How long do notifications live?
decisions.options: (a) A nightly pg_cron job deletes notifications older than 90 days; recipients and push_deliveries cascade. (b) Keep everything; the inbox only shows 90 days.
decisions.recommendation: (a). It matches the concept and the existing app_events / push_deliveries retention, and it also clears the old unread backlog (407 rows older than 90 days) before the first unread badge appears.

decisions.question: D-N12 When should iOS ask for notification permission (opt-in UX)?
decisions.options: (a) As now: only from the settings button or when Apple Health is connected. (b) Once after the first sign-in, with a one-line explainer and a Settings fallback, matching Android RootScreen.kt:79-90. (c) Provisional ('quiet') authorization.
decisions.recommendation: (b). It's one rule on both phones and explains the 10 iOS vs 19 Android tokens gap. Reminders/Digest stay off until the member turns them on in Notifications settings, with consent copy next to the switch and the switch as the opt-out (App Store 4.5.4).

decisions.question: D-N13 Should we turn on the stubbed program.updated / program.deleted notifications?
decisions.options: (a) Turn them on as the original app had them: all active members, including whoever made the edit. (b) Turn them on but exclude the person who made the change. (c) Leave them off.
decisions.recommendation: (b). People in a program learn about name, status and date changes, and the admin doesn't notify themselves. Note: old binaries will show these as modals, which is accepted because it was the original behavior.

decisions.question: D-N14 Do we add an app-icon unread badge?
decisions.options: (a) APNs badge = the server's unread count, which the app resets when the inbox opens. Only turned on after MIN_IOS_VERSION is raised to the inbox build, because 1.4.2 never clears a badge. (b) No icon badge; in-app badge only.
decisions.recommendation: (a), gated as described. It's the platform norm, and Android already shows launcher dots from tray notifications.

decisions.question: D-N15 Which store release carries the redesign?
decisions.options: (a) Fold it into the store submission you are holding for the polish pass. (b) Keep that submission to the polish items (e.g. the offline indicator). Backend slices go live whenever they're ready (they're additive), and the client inbox rides the next train.
decisions.recommendation: (b). Don't delay the reliability release (logouts, sync) behind a multi-surface feature.

build_slices: N1 - backend, S: category map in code (type -> category), so no column is needed; additive push keys (`category` in data, APNs `thread-id`); turn on the stubbed program.updated/deleted excluding the actor (services/programService.js:20-23); migration 011 (schema-neutral, staging then public) with the nightly 90-day notifications retention. Safe for every live binary.

N2 - backend, M: same migration 011 adds notification_preferences, members.time_zone and a unique notifications.dedupe_key. New routes GET /notifications (paged, 90 days, read flag + unread_count), POST /notifications/read-all, GET|PUT /notifications/preferences; X-Time-Zone capture middleware (store on change); createNotification filters push by preferences (D-N2). /unacknowledged and the SSE frames stay unchanged.

N3 - web, M: the picker actions sheet 'My Invites' becomes 'Inbox' (invites + history, mark-all-read) built with the frontend kit; the '+' button badge = unread + invites; a floating toast replaces the blocking NotificationModal; a new /program/notifications page under My Account with the switches + reminder time; X-Time-Zone header in apiRequest.

N4 - iOS, M (parallel with N5): the same Inbox in ProgramActionsSheet plus an Inbox row in the account section; toast instead of NotificationModalView; switches + time picker on NotificationsSettingsView; X-Time-Zone header; ask permission once after first sign-in; reset the badge count when the inbox opens. New code in new files (ProgramPickerView is already 982 lines).

N5 - Android, M (parallel with N4): the same Inbox in the picker actions sheet + account row; toast instead of the NotificationModal dialog; switches + M3 TimePicker on NotificationsScreen; X-Time-Zone header; new rasi_reminders channel (and rasi_digest later); monochrome small icon + default_notification_icon meta-data. New code in new files and a ViewModel, not in ProgramContext.kt (already 1,512 lines). Then compile check (Gradle) and the user's Cmd+B for iOS, then one train per phone.

N6 - backend, S-M: the in-process 15-minute reminder ticker (D-N8/D-N9) with dedupe_key, sending only to members with reminders on and a known time zone; all sends go through createNotification, so they are recorded in push_deliveries. Safe to deploy before the clients ship: with no opt-ins, nothing sends.
N7 - backend + 3 clients, S: after the inbox builds are adopted and MIN_IOS_VERSION / MIN_ANDROID versionCode are raised, turn on APNs badge = unread count (D-N14).

N8 - backend, M (optional follow-on): weekly Digest (Monday 09:00 local, opt-in, last week's workouts and minutes per program from analyticsService) on the same ticker, plus its preference switch on the 3 settings screens.
N9 - later, with the People layer: the Activity category (logs and kudos from people in your programs), opt-in or default to be decided then.
risks: OLD BINARIES (iOS 1.4.2 App Store, Android 1.0.0 Play) show every notification row as a blocking modal and still get its push. Any new type reaches them. Mitigation: Reminders/Digest/Activity can only be turned on from the new builds' settings, so old-app users never opt in. program.updated/deleted (D-N13) will show up as modals on old apps, which is accepted because it's the original behavior. Pin these as rules in the plan.
APP-ICON BADGE: sending an APNs badge before the version gate is raised leaves a stuck badge on 1.4.2, which never clears it. Keep N7 behind the MIN_IOS_VERSION raise.

FIRST-OPEN UNREAD SHOCK: 333 unread rows, up to 51 for one member. Retention (N1) must run before the inbox clients ship, or the first badge shows big numbers. If the remaining 90-day backlog still looks bad, mark it read in the migration (a user-run migration, never a direct write).

APP STORE 4.5.4 / PLAY: engagement pushes must be opt-in with consent copy and an in-app opt-out. A reminder that is on by default is a review risk. Never use iOS 'Time Sensitive' for reminders (it needs an entitlement). Play doesn't allow ads in system notifications, so the vestigial broadcast must not become a marketing channel without its own opt-in category.

SCHEDULER: it assumes the single Render instance (SSE has the same limit, F2). The dedupe_key unique index is what prevents double sends during deploy overlap or after scaling. Window-based catch-up must not send a 19:00 reminder at midnight after a long outage, so cap the window (e.g. 2 h).

TIME ZONE: members on old builds, web-only members with a wrong browser zone, and the 38 of 60 members with no device get little from reminders. On web a reminder only lands in the inbox (no web push, D-11), so reminders are effectively a phone feature.

FILE SIZE / LAYERING: Android ProgramContext.kt is already 1,512 lines and iOS ProgramPickerView.swift 982. Inbox and preference code must go in new modules (the CLAUDE.md ~200-line rule) or the three implementations will drift.

PARITY: three clients plus the backend are changing at once, which is exactly where Phase 3 needed a parity pass (8 cross-surface mismatches). Run the shared-amendments step before implementers start, and give D-N2 and D-N3 one written contract.

NOISE: member_joined is the noisiest type (245 recipient rows in 90 days). Moving from modal to toast + inbox cuts the interruption, but don't add Activity pushes until the People layer gives people a reason to want them.

SCOPE / TIMING: the user's current request is the iPhone offline indicator (they see endless loading instead of an immediate offline state; plan file specs/initiatives/reliability-overhaul/plans/polish-1-offline-detection.md is untracked). The store submission is on hold for polish. This notifications discovery should not delay that fix, and nothing here needs an App Store or Play upload now.
MIGRATIONS: 011 must be schema-neutral and the user runs it on staging, then public, before the backend deploy (board §8). The new pg_cron job names need the per-schema suffix pattern from sql/010.

candidates.screen: Program actions sheet (Invites + Create), widget quick-add forms, health confirmation
candidates.problem: The one offline banner is an overlay on AppRootView's ZStack (AppRootView.swift:47-51), so every sheet and full-screen cover hides it. Apply it to the roots of ProgramActionsSheet, both widget entry views and HealthSyncConfirmationView. Hide InvitesTab's stale banner while offline (ScreenBanner rule) and refetch the invites on reconnect. candidates.other_surfaces: On Android the widget forms are routes under RootScreen's OfflineBanner (RootScreen.kt:244-252), so they already show it. The Android ModalBottomSheet program actions sheet (ProgramActionsSheet.kt:98) has the same gap. Web has no sheets.

candidates.screen: Widget deep link → quick-add form (app root)
candidates.problem: onOpenURL awaits checkMinimumSupportedVersion(), a GET /app-config with a 15 s timeout, before it sets widgetRoute (AppRootView.swift:110-121). On weak or dead Wi-Fi, a widget tap shows nothing for up to 15 s. The foreground path also awaits the same call before sessionDidBecomeActive and the session restore (lines 80-86).
candidates.fix: Set widgetRoute right away and run the check in a separate Task. The existing onChange(isUpdateRequired) (lines 72-76) already closes the form if an update turns out to be required. Run the foreground check alongside sessionDidBecomeActive instead of before it.
candidates.benefit: The quick-add form opens instantly from the widget on any network, the 'it's just loading' symptom, and foreground refresh, sync and stream start one round-trip sooner.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android caps the widget gate at 3 s with withTimeoutOrNull(3_000) (RootScreen.kt:181-191; amendment A7), so iOS is the outlier. Web has no widgets.

(QuickAddWorkoutWidgetEntryView.swift:488-497; QuickAddHealthWidgetEntryView.swift:538), and SearchablePickerSheet has no empty state (SearchablePickerSheet.swift:18-35). candidates.problem: LoginView is a plain VStack in a ZStack with no ScrollView (LoginView.swift:20-138). It is the only auth screen without one: ForgotPasswordView.swift:24 has one, and CreateAccountView.swift:53-54 added one specifically to fix 'fields vanish' under the keyboard. The content is roughly 640 pt (logo, title, 2 fields, button, 2 social buttons, 3 footer rows), more than an iPhone SE's roughly 600 pt usable height. Likely result: fields clip with the keyboard up or at large Dynamic Type. This is an estimate and needs a check on a device.
candidates.fix: Wrap the VStack in a ScrollView with .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively) and .scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize), the same recipe as CreateAccountView.
candidates.benefit: The sign-in form always fits and the focused field stays visible on small iPhones and with large text.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android AuthScaffold scrolls (AuthComponents.kt:97-104). Web is a normal scrolling page.

candidates.screen: Login, Create account, My Profile (email / add password)
candidates.problem: No iOS field sets .textContentType (a grep finds no matches), so Password AutoFill and strong-password suggestions can't target the right fields. Web sets autocomplete username/current-password/new-password/email/given-name (login/page.tsx:171,184; create-account/page.tsx:290-407). The email fields get the default keyboard: CreateAccountView.swift:204 passes no keyboardType, and MyProfileView.swift:204-205 applies .keyboardType(.emailAddress) outside AppInputField, whose inner .keyboardType(.default) (AppInputField.swift:19-20) very likely wins. Pressing Return on the login password field does not submit.
candidates.fix: Add a contentType parameter to AppInputField and set .username/.password/.newPassword/.emailAddress/.givenName/.familyName. Pass keyboardType: .emailAddress through the parameter. Add .onSubmit { handleLogin } on login. Optional follow-up (M): a webcredentials associated domain plus an apple-app-site-association file on rasifiters.com, so Keychain suggests saved site logins.
candidates.benefit: Password managers and iCloud Keychain can fill sign-in and suggest a strong password at sign-up, and email fields get an '@' keyboard. Less friction on the most-used form.
candidates.other_surfaces: Web already has autocomplete hints. Android sets KeyboardType.Email on profile email (ProfileScreen.kt:235) but no autofill hints in auth (worth checking there too).

candidates.benefit: Removes a 6-second wait every time someone has to sign in again.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android has the same typewriter gate (SplashScreen.kt:46-64, 117), although its forced sign-out lands on Login. The web root is the landing page with an immediate button.

candidates.problem: CreateProgramTabView only requires a name (lines 21-23) and lets the end date fall before the start date. The backend does not validate (programService.js:93-107), so such a program shows a 0% progress bar forever (ProgramPickerView.swift:943-948 and the server's progress CASE).
candidates.fix: Copy Edit's dateRangeError ('End date must be after the start date.') into Create and add it to the button's disabled condition. Note it in program-actions SPEC (supersedes F5).
candidates.benefit: Prevents creating broken programs from the iPhone.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android already validates on create. Web create (programs/page.tsx:1022-1081) lacks it, so the same small fix applies there.

candidates.problem: identities defaults to [] and hasPassword to true (MyProfileView.swift:33-34), and loadIdentities swallows errors (lines 293-295). Before the load finishes, or when offline, Google and Apple read 'Not linked' with an enabled Link button (lines 271-287), which is false state.
candidates.fix: Make it three-state: loading shows '—' with the buttons disabled; failure shows an inline kit message with Retry and hides Link/Unlink; loaded shows today's UI.
candidates.benefit: Users never see a wrong account status or try to link an account that is already linked.
candidates.other_surfaces: Same pattern on web (program/profile/page.tsx:227-229) and Android (ProfileScreen.kt:94, 121).

candidates.problem: The paged TabView (CreateAccountView.swift:80-87) can be swiped past the Continue gates, and submit checks only canContinue(lastStep) (lines 389-401, 425-433). Blank names or an invalid email reach the server and come back as a 400 alert. If register succeeds but the auto-login fails, the next tap registers again and gets 'Username already exists' (lines 440-459; spec F2).
candidates.fix: On submit, require every page to pass canContinue and jump to the first page that fails. Keep a didRegister flag so a retry only signs in. On a final login failure, say 'Account created, please sign in'.
candidates.benefit: No confusing server errors, and no misleading 'username taken' message after the account was in fact created.
candidates.other_surfaces: Web and Android have the same register-then-login gap (create-account/page.tsx:188-202; CreateAccountScreen.kt:95-101). Their wizards are button-driven, so the swipe half is iOS-only.

candidates.screen: Login / Create account / Change password / Program picker / Invites / Apple Health / Appearance / widget forms
candidates.problem: (1) The eye toggle has no label and a tap target of about 22 pt (AppInputField.swift:40-47); Android says 'Show/Hide password' (AuthComponents.kt:211). candidates.other_surfaces: Android covers (1) and the confirm tick via contentDescription. The other items were not checked on Android or web.

candidates.screen: Log workout / Log daily health (and every save/edit/delete in the area)
candidates.problem: TanStack's default networkMode 'online' pauses mutations after a browser 'offline' event, so isPending stays true and Save reads 'Saving…' indefinitely (providers.tsx:32 sets only retry:false; LogWorkoutsForm.tsx:535, LogDailyHealthForm.tsx:608). When a save does fail, ~20 call sites show raw text via (error as Error).message: summary/page.tsx:317,336; log-workout:59; log-health:59; members/workouts:144,162; members/health:166,181; members/detail:69,84; lifestyle/workouts:62-102; program/page.tsx:86; program/edit:81; program/roles:72. Users see 'Load failed', 'Request timed out' or 'Request failed (500)'.
candidates.fix: Set mutations: { retry: false, networkMode: "always" } in providers.tsx so an offline save fails at once. Route every mutation error through toAppError(error).message, which keeps the server text for 400s and row errors (duplicate name, 'has N logs', batch row errors).
candidates.benefit: Saving with no connection shows 'Can't connect. Check your internet connection and try again.' right away, not an endless 'Saving…' or browser jargon. This is the behavior the user asked for.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS AddWorkoutsDetailView.swift:466-467 shows error.localizedDescription and Android LogWorkoutScreen.kt:202-204 shows e.message, so both have raw text too. Neither has the paused-forever problem.

candidates.screen: Members > View Workouts and View Health edit modals; Lifestyle > Workout Types add/edit modals
candidates.problem:
Validation and save errors go to a page-level

behind the open z-50 modal. members/workouts: errors set at :204 and :162, shown at :247, modal at :399-475. members/health: set at :262-270 and :166, shown at :317, modal at :504-593. lifestyle/workouts: set at :82 and :94, shown at :147, modals at :189-258. Saving with an empty duration, or adding a duplicate workout name (400 'A workout with this name already exists in the program.'), looks like nothing happened.
candidates.fix: Show the error inside each modal above its buttons and clear it on close. Disable Save while the input is invalid, as iOS does.
candidates.benefit: Users see why Save didn't work instead of tapping a button that seems dead.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS shows the error inside the sheet (MemberRecentDetail.swift:801-805, MemberHealthDetail.swift:946-949) and disables Save while invalid. Android not verified.

candidates.screen: 13 detail screens: Summary activity/distribution/workout-types; Members list/detail/metrics/history/streaks/workouts/health; Lifestyle timeline/steps/workout-types; Program roles
candidates.problem: These screens use isLoading → LoadingState and isError → ErrorState((error as Error).message) (e.g. summary/activity:39-45, members/history:58-60, lifestyle/timeline:63-67). After an 'offline' event the query is paused: isLoading and isError are both false and there is no data, so the page is blank under its header. When the link is up but there is no internet, it ends in a raw 'Load failed' / 'Failed to fetch' with no Retry. members/workouts (:249-253), members/health (:319-323) and lifestyle/workouts (:149) have no error branch at all. members/detail renders nothing for an unknown member (:98).
candidates.fix: Use the kit recipe already on Summary: const s = fromQuery(q) → LoadingState / <ErrorView error onRetry={() => q.refetch()} /> / content, plus a stale FloatingBanner hidden while offline. A tiny shared wrapper keeps each page to about 5 lines. Add a 'member not found' message on members/detail.
candidates.benefit: Every drill-down shows 'Couldn't load this · Can't connect…' with Retry instead of a blank page or browser jargon. This is also needed for polish-1: once the app knows it is offline, fromQuery already maps a paused query with no data to the offline error.
candidates.other_surfaces: Same gap on iOS and Android. Only the picker and Summary use the kit there (iOS ProgramPickerView / AdminSummaryTab / InvitesTabView; Android ProgramPickerScreen / SummaryScreen). iOS ActivityTimelineDetailView shows a raw errorMessage.

candidates.screen: Log workout / Log daily health forms
candidates.problem: Member, workout-type and program lookups load in an effect whose catch swallows the error (LogWorkoutsForm.tsx:147-158, LogDailyHealthForm.tsx:174-175). If they fail, the form says 'No workout types available for this program yet.' or 'No active members in this program yet.' (LogWorkoutsForm.tsx:315-320, LogDailyHealthForm.tsx:368). The dropdowns are empty and the only way to retry is to close the form.
candidates.fix: Keep a lookup error in state and show the kit ErrorView (offline/timeout copy plus a Retry that re-runs the lookup load) in place of the 'none yet' hint.
candidates.benefit: Someone logging on a weak connection is told the real problem and can retry, instead of being told the program has no workouts or members.
candidates.other_surfaces: Not verified on iOS (ProgramContext.loadLookupData) or Android.

candidates.screen: Members detail/invite/history/streaks/workouts/health, Program edit/roles, Log workout/health pages
candidates.problem: Role-redirect effects run on the first render, before AuthProvider restores the session. The session starts null (auth-provider.tsx:53), and child effects run before the provider's bootstrap effect (:211-226). On a reload or a shared link, isGlobalAdmin and loggedInUserId are still empty, so the page redirects away. A plain member reloading /members/history?memberId=<self> is sent to /members (history:37-42; same in streaks:27-32, workouts:70-75, health:85-90). A global admin reloading /members/detail always bounces (detail:32-36). Same for invite:21-25, program/edit:34-38, roles:28-32 and log-workout:26-30 for global admins who are not program admins.
candidates.fix: Skip these redirects until !isBootstrapping. useAuthGuard already returns it, so it is one condition per effect.
candidates.benefit: Pull-to-refresh on mobile Safari, a browser refresh or a bookmarked link keeps the user on the page they were on.
candidates.other_surfaces: Web only (the native apps have no URL reloads).

candidates.problem: Sorting by 'Avg Steps' (metrics/page.tsx:28) labels each card's hero number 'Avg Steps', but heroValue has no avg_steps case and falls back to metric.workouts (:242-263). The big number is the workout count.
candidates.fix: Add case "avg_steps": return stepsLabel(metric.avg_steps ?? null).
candidates.benefit: Admins who sort by steps see steps, not a mislabeled workout count.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS (MemberOverviewPicker.swift:311) and Android (MemberCards.kt:105) handle avg_steps correctly, so this is web only.

candidates.problem: Six queries with no error handling (members/page.tsx:68-198). When any of them fails or is paused offline: the metrics preview says 'Loading...' forever (:291); the overview says 'No workouts logged yet.' (:579-581); streaks show '0 days' (:345-346); daily average shows 0.0 (:341); the recent and health cards say there are no logs (:728, :758); and the View-as picker is empty. The same false empty states flash on every member switch while loading.
candidates.fix: Apply the Summary pattern (summary/page.tsx:162-168, :222, :345-352): fromQuery per query, one ErrorView + Retry when something failed with no data, '—' for missing values, and the stale banner. Show '…' instead of 'No workouts logged yet.' while a card loads.
candidates.benefit: The Members tab never says a member has no workouts or a 0-day streak when the data just didn't load.
candidates.other_surfaces: Same on iOS and Android (Android MembersScreen.kt:63 'load errors swallowed — iOS F1'). The iOS program-member-management SPEC F1 already lists this as a cleanup candidate.

candidates.screen: Members > Performance Metrics (also View Workouts / View Health sort and filter)
candidates.problem: The search text is part of the query key and is sent to the server (metrics/page.tsx:121-131; lib/api/members.ts:117) with no debounce and no previous-data retention. Every keystroke fires a request, the list is replaced by 'Loading metrics...' (:213) and the subtitle flips to 'Loading metrics...' (:176). members/workouts (:104-130) and members/health (:119-151) blank the same way on every sort or filter change.
candidates.fix: Add placeholderData: keepPreviousData to these three queries, plus a ~250 ms debounce on the metrics search.
candidates.benefit: Typing a name filters smoothly without the list blinking out, with far fewer requests.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS (MemberMetricsDetailView.swift:70 onCommit) and Android (MemberMetricsDetailScreen.kt:154 onSearch) search on submit, so they don't flicker.

candidates.screen: All sub-pages (Back), row actions, modal Done/Close, period selectors
candidates.problem: Common controls are well under the kit's 44pt minimum: the Back pill on every sub-page is px-3 py-1 text-xs, about 26px (BackButton.tsx:9); row Edit/Delete/Hide pills are about 24px (members/workouts:270-283, members/health:340-353, lifestyle/workouts:318-340), and so are modal Done/Close; View-as picker rows are py-2, about 36px (members/page.tsx:816, :828). The W/M/Y/P buttons have no accessible name or pressed state (PeriodSelector.tsx:24-31), so screen readers just say 'W'.
candidates.fix: Give BackButton, Button size 'sm' and these pills min-h-[44px] (more padding, same font). Add aria-label (Week/Month/Year/Program) and aria-pressed to PeriodSelector.
candidates.benefit: Fewer mis-taps on phones and period switching that works with VoiceOver.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS and Android use native controls with platform-sized hit areas.

candidates.problem: Lifestyle shows a failed or paused query as missing data: 'N/A' / 'No data' (lifestyle/page.tsx:238-282), 'No data yet.' (:403-407, :495-499), 'No workouts logged yet.' (:560-562). The Program tab shows '0 active' (program/page.tsx:154, :297), 'No admins or loggers assigned.' (:188-192) and '0 types available' (:233-237) when its two queries fail.
candidates.fix: Same Summary-style adoption: one ErrorView + Retry when a query failed with no data, '—' instead of the false values, and the stale banner.
candidates.benefit: Admins aren't told their program has no members, roles or workout types because of a dropped connection.
candidates.other_surfaces: Same on iOS and Android (Android LifestyleScreen.kt:48 'load errors swallowed').

candidates.problem: Only a failed query shows '—'. While loading with no cache (the first open of a program), Program Progress shows 0%, 0/0 days and 0 days (summary/page.tsx:387-440), Activity shows 'Daily avg 0.0' (:235), and Workout Types says 'No workouts logged yet.' (:620-621). That last one also appears under the ErrorView when its query failed. The status badge falls back to 'active' even when the analytics query failed (:432).
candidates.fix: Treat 'loading' like 'failed' in these fallbacks ('—' or '…'). Show the Workout Types empty text only when that query loaded empty.
candidates.benefit: No misleading zeros or 'no workouts' on first open or under an error, in line with the kit's no-fake-zeros rule (D-KIT-13).
candidates.other_surfaces: Not verified on iOS/Android.

candidates.problem: The 'Active Membership' checkbox (members/detail/page.tsx:132-142) sends is_active:false, which the backend turns into status 'removed' (membershipService.js:221-223). That is a removal with no confirmation and without removeMember's cleanup: no removed-member notification and no invite revocation (:328-345). The member then disappears from the roster, because details returns only active rows (:150). The list's 'Inactive' badge (members/list:97-101) can therefore never show, and the member can't be reactivated from the UI.
candidates.fix: Remove the checkbox and keep the Joined Program date. 'Remove from program' already covers removal, with a confirm step. Delete the dead Inactive badge.

candidates.screen: Log forms, member log edit/delete, member editor, roles, workout types, edit/leave program
candidates.problem: Every write in this area shows e.message raw. asApiError maps only HttpException (core/ProgramContext.kt:1458), so a server error reads 'Request failed (500)' (net/ApiException.kt:28) and an offline save shows OkHttp's 'Unable to resolve host … No address associated with hostname'. Affected sites: LogWorkoutScreen.kt:204, LogHealthScreen.kt:230, MemberRecentDetailScreen.kt:191,207, MemberHealthDetailScreen.kt:191,208, MemberManagementScreens.kt:290,318, ManageRolesScreen.kt:91, WorkoutTypesListScreen.kt:94, EditProgramScreen.kt:158, ProgramScreen.kt:143. Only Invite and Profile go through the kit.
candidates.fix: Replace `it.message ?: …` with `it.toAppError().message` at those sites. The kit already keeps the server's text for 400/422 and for batch rowErrors, so row highlighting and validation messages are unchanged.
candidates.benefit: Errors read the same everywhere in plain words ('Can't connect. Check your internet connection…') instead of OS or HTTP jargon, which matters most when logging offline.
candidates.other_surfaces: All three have it. iOS uses error.localizedDescription (AddWorkoutsDetailView.swift:467, MemberRecentDetail.swift:422,824). Web passes (error as Error).message (web app/summary/page.tsx:317,336, app/summary/log-workout/page.tsx:59).

candidates.problem: The lookups handle only success (LogWorkoutScreen.kt:143-149, LogHealthScreen.kt:162-165) and then set lookupsLoaded = true. Offline, the form says 'No workout types available for this program yet.' (LogWorkoutScreen.kt:246) or 'No active members in this program yet.' (:248) and the pickers are empty. The user is told the program is misconfigured and can't log anything.
candidates.fix: Track a lookup error. When set, the hint row shows the kit message and a Retry link that re-runs both lookups, instead of the empty-catalog text.
candidates.benefit: The most-used write flow gives the right explanation and one-tap recovery when offline.
candidates.other_surfaces: Web shows the same string whenever the lookups are empty (web components/forms/LogWorkoutsForm.tsx:315-320). iOS not checked.

candidates.problem: Add, edit, delete and hide/show each run the write and `loadAllProgramWorkouts().getOrThrow()` in one runCatching (core/ProgramContext.kt:1308-1340). If the write lands but the reload fails, the UI reports a failure. Hide/Show is a server-side toggle (backend services/workoutService.js:126-141), so the natural re-tap flips it back. A re-tapped Add gets 'A workout with this name already exists' (:152). The error is also drawn on the page behind the add/edit sheet (WorkoutTypesListScreen.kt:92-95,122-125); the sheet has no error slot or in-flight state, so Add looks like it did nothing.
candidates.fix: Use the write's own result as the outcome and make the reload best-effort, as iOS does. Show errors and a spinner inside WorkoutNameSheet, and disable Confirm while saving.
candidates.benefit: On flaky networks admins no longer accidentally reverse a hide/show or hit duplicate-name errors, and they can see why an add failed.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS is not affected because its reload doesn't throw (ProgramContext+WorkoutManagement.swift:110,123). Web not checked.

candidates.problem: loadLifestyle runs 7 GETs one after another inside one runCatching (core/ProgramContext.kt:1267-1281), so a single failure discards all seven. lifestyleLoading (:1229) is never read, so there is no loading state. The LifestyleData defaults (:1480) render 'Total workout types 0', 'N/A / No data', 'No workouts logged yet.' and 'No data yet' (LifestyleCards.kt:107-130, 208-213, 348-355) while loading or after a failure. Switching View-as shows the previous member's stats under the new name until all seven calls finish. No pull-to-refresh, although DESIGN_BOARD §6.6 asks for it.
candidates.fix: Mirror loadSummary: run the reads in parallel and keep per-part results in UiState<LifestyleData>. Show '…' while loading and '—' for a failed part (as web does). Show ErrorView with Retry when nothing loaded, and the stale banner otherwise. Wrap the tab in PullToRefreshBox and delete the unused lifestyleLoading.
candidates.benefit: The tab opens after one network wait instead of seven in sequence (DESIGN_BOARD §6.5 budget; matters for the East-Africa users) and never shows fake zeros or another member's numbers.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS uses the same pattern (AdminWorkoutTypesTab.swift:135-148: serial loads, cards fed `?? 0`). Web already shows '…'/'—' per card (web app/lifestyle/page.tsx:218-231).

candidates.screen: Activity, Distribution, Member History, Member Streaks, Lifestyle Timeline, Steps Timeline
candidates.problem: Six drill-downs are plain Columns with no verticalScroll (ActivityDetailScreen.kt:62-67, DistributionDetailScreen.kt:39-44, MemberSimpleDetails.kt:59-63 and 143-147, LifestyleTimelineDetailScreen.kt:80-84, StepsTimelineDetailScreen.kt:78-82). Each holds about 300dp of header plus a fixed 320-360dp chart and legend, roughly 660dp in total. On a 360×740 phone with 3-button navigation the tab content area is about 590dp (about 510dp while the offline reserve is on, AppScaffold.kt:140). The bottom of the chart and the legend are cut off and can't be reached, and a larger font scale makes it worse.
candidates.fix: Add `.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())` to each Column, or give the chart weight(1f) with a minimum height.
candidates.benefit: Charts fit on budget phones, which are likely common in this app's general audience, and at large text sizes.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android only. iOS charts flex (minHeight 240 inside the VStack) and web pages scroll.

candidates.problem: The standard view runs 7 reads one after another behind a single spinner (ui/members/MembersScreen.kt:160-174). The admin view runs 5 reads one after another with no loading state (:103-112). Failures are swallowed by design (members SPEC: 'Read-only tab (iOS F1)'), so cards show '0 days' streaks (MemberCards.kt:447-448), 'No workouts logged yet.' (:230) and '0 members / No members to display' (:365-376).
candidates.fix: Small step now: run the reads concurrently (coroutineScope { launch … }) and show '—' instead of 0 when a value is null. Leave the full kit treatment to the People rebuild (DESIGN_BOARD §10: the Members tab becomes People, built with the W7 kit) so it isn't built twice.
candidates.benefit: The Members tab opens after one network wait instead of five to seven in sequence, and stops showing fake zero streaks.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS swallows errors the same way (it is the F1 original). Web runs its queries in parallel with isLoading placeholders (web app/members/page.tsx:297).

candidates.screen: Member log lists, log forms, period/metric selectors, Manage Roles, metrics search
candidates.problem:
Several controls are well under 48dp:
- ⋮ actions are 22dp (MemberRecentDetailScreen.kt:256, MemberHealthDetailScreen.kt:257), while the same menu in WorkoutTypesListScreen uses a 48dp IconButton.
- 'Remove entry' in the log forms is 28dp (LogWorkoutScreen.kt:345, LogHealthScreen.kt:375).
- Search-clear is 20dp (MemberMetricsDetailScreen.kt:149).
- The W/M/Y/P and Count/Minutes segments are about 38dp clickable Boxes with no selected or Tab semantics, so TalkBack can't tell which is selected (DetailChrome.kt:244-252, the duplicate in MemberSimpleDetails.kt:199-207, LifestyleCards.kt:292-320).
- Role pills are about 36dp (ManageRolesScreen.kt:157).
candidates.fix: Use IconButton or Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize() for the icons. On the shared PeriodSelector and MetricSegmented, add `Modifier.selectable(selected, role = Role.Tab)` and heightIn(min = 48.dp). Delete the duplicate HistoryPeriodSelector.
candidates.benefit: Fewer mis-taps on small icons, and TalkBack announces the selected period.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS uses system segmented Pickers and swipe actions (44pt targets). Web not checked.

candidates.problem: The Delete dialog stays open and enabled while the request runs (MemberRecentDetailScreen.kt:203-209, MemberHealthDetailScreen.kt:203-209), so a double tap sends two DELETEs. The second one gets 404 'Workout log not found.' (backend services/logService.js:497-498) and pops 'Something went wrong' after a successful delete. 'Save changes' in the edit sheets has no loading state (MemberRecentDetailScreen.kt:377, MemberHealthDetailScreen.kt:392), so there is no feedback for up to the 15 s timeout.
candidates.fix: Add a busy flag: disable Delete and Save while the call runs and show PillButton(loading = true) until it returns.
candidates.benefit: No false error after a successful delete, and users can see a save is in progress.
candidates.other_surfaces: Not checked on iOS or web.

candidates.screen: Program tab (admin), View Members roster, Manage Roles, Workout Types
candidates.problem:
These screens load once and show nothing useful when the load fails:
- Roster: just the search field (MemberManagementScreens.kt:158,185).
- Manage Roles: an empty card (ManageRolesScreen.kt:57,77).
- Workout Types: a blank list (WorkoutTypesListScreen.kt:85,138).
- Program tab: '0 enrolled', 'No admins or loggers assigned' and '0 types available' (ProgramSections.kt:173,198,264) until its 3 reads succeed (ProgramScreen.kt:71-77).
None has pull-to-refresh, so the only way to retry is to leave the screen.
candidates.fix: Give each screen a small UiState: a spinner while loading, the kit ErrorView with Retry when the load fails with no data, and an explicit empty line otherwise. Show '—' for the Program-tab counts until they load. Wrap each screen in PullToRefreshBox (DESIGN_BOARD §6.6).
candidates.benefit: Admins can tell 'nobody here' from 'couldn't load' and can retry without leaving the screen.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS has pull-to-refresh on all three management sections (MemberManagementSection.swift:106, WorkoutTypesSection.swift:145, RoleManagementSection.swift:221); its error states were not checked.

candidates.problem: Workouts and Health fetch with limit=0, which returns every row because the backend applies a limit only when it is above 0 (backend services/memberAnalyticsService.js:400-401). They render with items.forEach inside a scrolling Column (MemberRecentDetailScreen.kt:143, MemberHealthDetailScreen.kt:145), and the metrics cards do the same, so every row and its dropdown Box is built at once. A failed reload keeps the old list, or the tab's 10-row preview, under a new sort or 'Filter •' label. A failed first load says 'No workouts found. Adjust filters or log a workout…'.
candidates.fix: Move the three lists to LazyColumn, with the header and controls as items and rows keyed. Drive them with UiState: ErrorView when there is no data, the stale banner when old data is kept.
candidates.benefit: Members with long histories scroll smoothly on budget phones, and failures no longer look like 'no results'.
candidates.other_surfaces: iOS uses a lazy List (MemberRecentDetail.swift:317, MemberHealthDetail.swift:320). Web not checked.

candidates.problem: MemberPickerSheet sizes its list at 48dp per row (ui/members/MembersScreen.kt:342), but each PickerRow is about 52dp (14dp×2 padding plus a 24sp bodyLarge line, :373-378). With 6 or fewer members the last row is clipped by about 4dp per row and needs an inner scroll. It gets worse at larger font scales.
candidates.fix: Use heightIn(max = 380.dp) and let the LazyColumn wrap its content, as SearchablePickerField already does (ui/summary/DetailChrome.kt:195).
candidates.benefit: The picker always shows every member in full at any font size.
candidates.other_surfaces: Android only (iOS uses a List sheet).
